doc.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Keepnews on being a producer and a catalytic agent
summary: He prefers to be remembered as a producer and defines the job as creating circumstances in which the artist can work best.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I tend to think of myself primarily at least as a producer, and that’s the way I would prefer to be remembered. If I were to have a gravestone that’s what it should — if it gives occupation on gravestones, that’s what I want.
Right. Well I have to congratulate you on the contribution you’ve made to the art form called jazz. It’s really quite amazing the things you’ve been involved in and the careers that you have helped.

Well I must admit that I look back on it with a good deal of satisfaction. I’ve been very fortunate because in this business in particular, a lot of the associations that you form, at least initially, are accidental as hell. If someone tells me that I have been helpful to this or that career that’s exactly the thing that I want to hear because I have always looked on the role of the producer in a very specific way. Now one of the hardest things, and I’ve been at it, I’m getting perilously close to my fiftieth anniversary in this business, but I still have to pause usually when I’m asked to make some kind of definition of what it is I do, because for better or worse, I don’t know about other things because I’ve only done this really, but jazz record producers do a little bit of everything, as there is always a shortage of personnel, and it’s to me, the most important role is what I have taken to repetitiously referring to as being a catalytic agent. That I am supposed to create the circumstances under which the artist can work most effectively. That is, I’ve finally got it boiled down to that one mantra and that’s what I am, that’s what I do. I think one of the great things about — that statement is generally true, but the details of its implementation are constantly changing. There are no — almost literally — there are no two artists who can be dealt with in the same way. There are perhaps no two record dates that can be dealt with in the same way. That may be pushing it a little bit, but fundamentally that to me is what the continuing challenge is all about, that’s why I didn’t get bored a long time ago
